Humanitarian Assistance Program

HyperBurner’s real-world utility is transparent global humanitarian assistance.

🌍Our purpose

HyperBurner’s utility is humanitarian assistance: helping people in need around the world, with transparency at the core.

🤝How it works

Funding comes from the 500,000 HB left after the Holder Airdrop. 350,000 HB is staked, and all staking rewards go to the program. See how it is funded below.

🔍Transparency and reporting

Project 1

School Feeding & Learning Support Project

Community School Nourishment & Learning Boost

Goal
Improve attendance, concentration, and learning outcomes for primary school children.
Target group
200–400 pupils in 2–3 primary schools + their families.
Key activities
  • Establish a daily school meal program (fortified porridge or rice + beans).
  • Distribute termly learning kits (books, pens, solar lamps, reusable sanitary pads).
  • Set up school gardens managed by pupils and parents.
  • Run weekly after-school remedial classes.

Project 2

Maternal & Child Health Support Project

Safe Mothers, Healthy Babies Initiative

Goal
Reduce maternal and infant risks through better nutrition, care, and knowledge.
Target group
100–150 pregnant women and nursing mothers in a defined community.
Key activities
  • Monthly antenatal/postnatal outreach days with community health workers.
  • Distribution of mother kits (mosquito net, hygiene items, clean delivery supplies, fortified food).
  • Peer support groups for breastfeeding and nutrition education.
  • Transport support or accompaniment to health facilities for high-risk cases.

Project 3

Community Food Security & Household Resilience Project

Hunger-Free Households Program

Goal
Improve food access and reduce seasonal hunger for vulnerable households.
Target group
80–120 struggling households.
Key activities
  • Establish a community kitchen / food distribution point.
  • Support backyard/container gardening with free seeds and training.
  • Create a small community grain bank.
  • Cash-for-work or food-for-work for short-term income during lean seasons.

Project 4

Girl Child Protection & Empowerment Project

Safe Girls, Strong Futures

Goal
Protect girls from early marriage, violence, and school dropout while building their confidence and skills.
Target group
100–150 girls aged 10–18 + their parents/community leaders.
Key activities
  • Weekly safe-space sessions (life skills, reproductive health, rights education).
  • Mentorship with older female role models.
  • Community dialogues with parents, men, and traditional leaders.
  • School re-enrollment support and small economic activities for girls/mothers.

Project 5

Youth Micro-Enterprise & Low-Tech Skills Project

Youth Opportunity Hubs

Goal
Equip young people with practical skills and small capital to start income-generating activities.
Target group
50–80 youth (18–30 years), including low-level tech builders.
Key activities
  • Practical skills training (phone repair, solar installation, basic digital skills, agri-processing, tailoring, etc.).
  • Shared workspace / maker space with basic tools and solar power.
  • Micro-grants or revolving loans for the best business ideas.
  • Mentorship and market-linkage support.

Project 6

Integrated Community Health & Development Project

Healthy Communities Initiative

Goal
Improve basic health, water, sanitation, and community organization in one neighborhood or village cluster.
Target group
Entire community (e.g., 300–600 households).
Key activities
  • Train and equip community health workers.
  • Improve water points and household sanitation.
  • Regular health outreach and education campaigns.
  • Participatory community action planning and small infrastructure projects.

AIRDROP RULES • PUBLISHED BEFORE LAUNCH

Fair rules, written first.

Every rule below is public before a single HB is distributed, so nobody has to guess how a snapshot works.

WHEN A MILESTONE COUNTS24 hours above target

Market cap is the HB price on the main HB/SOL pool multiplied by circulating supply (5,000,000 minus burned HB, so 3,400,000 HB). We read it from DexScreener. A milestone is confirmed only after it stays above the target for 24 hours in a row.

WHO QUALIFIES2,000 HB for 7 days

A wallet must hold at least 2,000 HB, and keep that balance for the 7 days before the snapshot. Wallets count one by one, so splitting tokens across many wallets does not add up.

WHO IS EXCLUDEDPool, burn, project

The liquidity pool and its vaults, the burn address, and the project's airdrop and community wallets, plus any exchange-owned wallets. The full list is published before the first snapshot.

HOW REWARDS SPLITProportional, 2% cap

Each qualifying wallet gets a share in proportion to its HB balance. No wallet can receive more than 2% of a milestone pool (5,000 / 3,000 / 4,000 HB). Anything left from capped wallets is shared among the others.

WHERE THE TOKENS WAITPublic multisig wallet

The 1,100,000 HB airdrop pool is held in a multisig wallet with a public address. Snapshot data and distribution transactions are published after each payout.

CAMPAIGN POOL150,000 HB, no marketing wallet

Campaign rewards are paid only from the airdrop pool. Category amounts are announced before each campaign opens, the total can never exceed 150,000 HB, and no new HB is ever created.

WORKED EXAMPLE

How one share is calculated

The numbers below are only an illustration of the method.

01 Qualifying wallets together hold 400,000 HB02 One wallet holds 4,000 HB, which is 1% of that03 At the $1M snapshot it receives 1% of 250,000 HB04 Result: 2,500 HB, under the 5,000 HB cap

Airdrops depend on the market-cap milestones being reached and are not guaranteed. HB is a community token, not an investment, and its price can fall to zero. These rules are final once published. Any change is announced publicly before the next snapshot is scheduled, and never alters a snapshot that has already been taken.
